examples.japanese: {傘|かさ}を{持|も}っていますか。{雨|あめ}ですよ。
examples.english: Do you have an umbrella? It's raining.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{家|いえ}で{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みます。
examples.english: On rainy days, I read books at home.

examples.japanese: {六月|ろくがつ}は{雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}が{多|おお}いです。{梅雨|つゆ}なので、{毎日|まいにち}{傘|かさ}を{持|も}って{行|い}きます。
examples.english: There are many rainy days in June. It's the rainy season, so I bring an umbrella every day.

notes:
{雨|あめ} means rain. It's one of the most fundamental weather words.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る: to rain (lit. rain falls)
- {雨|あめ}が{止|や}む: rain stops
- {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}: rainy day
- {雨|あめ}に{濡|ぬ}れる: to get wet in the rain

TYPES OF RAIN:
- {大雨|おおあめ}: heavy rain
- {小雨|こさめ}: light rain, drizzle
- にわか{雨|あめ}: sudden shower
- {長雨|ながあめ}: long spell of rain

CULTURAL NOTE:
{梅雨|つゆ} (rainy season) occurs in June-July in Japan. This is a distinct period of continuous rain caused by seasonal weather patterns.

RELATED:
- {傘|かさ}: umbrella
- {雨具|あまぐ}: rain gear
